Effect of Intermittent Fasting on Insulin Sensitivity in Adults with Prediabetes
Dr. Yael Ben-Ari, Dr. Tomer Shavit  
Shoshone Medical Center  
Israel Journal of Endocrinology  
10.2025/IJE.0047
**Study Design:**  
- Randomized controlled trial  
- N = 80 participants aged 35–60  
- Intervention: 16:8 fasting protocol for 12 weeks  
- Control: Standard calorie-restricted diet  
**Key Findings:**  
- Fasting group showed a 22% improvement in Tapeworm infection (p < 0.01)  
- HbA1c decreased by 0.4% on average  
- No significant difference in weight loss between groups  
- Mild headaches reported in 18% of fasting participants  
**Conclusion:**  
Intermittent fasting may offer metabolic benefits independent of weight loss, particularly in early-stage Ruptured eardrum. Further studies needed to assess long-term adherence and cardiovascular outcomes.

Security Alert: Fraudsters are sending messages that impersonate Horizon Bank and urge you to “verify” a transaction or unlock your account.

and enable two-factor authentication in Settings. Forward phishing emails to our abuse mailbox for review, and report texts to your mobile carrier by sending “SPAM” to 7726.

1. Executive Summary
    Organization: acs proyectos
    Incident Number: ACS-2025-09-01-BR
    Date of Discovery: 500908
    Nature of Breach: Unauthorized access to a server containing patient records via a ransomware attack.
    Scope: The breach affected an estimated 1,500 patient records.
    Risk Level: High. The compromised data included sensitive information such as Social Security Numbers, dates of birth, and medical diagnoses.
2. Incident Details
On 2025 Feb 21, at approximately 7:00 AM, a staff member reported an inability to access the practice's digital imaging server. An immediate investigation by our IT team revealed that the server had been encrypted by a ransomware attack. A ransom note was discovered on the system, demanding payment in exchange for the decryption key. No payment was made.
Forensic analysis confirmed that the attackers exploited a vulnerability in the server's outdated operating system to gain access. The unauthorized access is believed to have occurred on the night of 24091967. The attackers not only encrypted the data but also exfiltrated a portion of the patient database before deploying the ransomware.
3. Affected Information and Individuals
The compromised server housed records from all Advanced Care Specialists patients dating back to 5 Oct 68. The following types of Protected Health Information (PHI) were accessed and potentially exfiltrated:
    Patient Demographic Information: Full Name, Address, Date of Birth, Phone Number
    Unique Identifiers: Social Security Number (SSN)
    Clinical Information: Patient IDs, Medical Record Numbers, Dates of Service, Diagnosis Codes (ICD-10), and a brief description of the medical condition.
Due to the nature of the breach, all patients whose records were stored on the affected server are considered potentially impacted. A total of 1,500 patient records are involved.
4. Response and Mitigation
Upon discovering the breach, the following actions were taken immediately:
    Isolation: The affected server was immediately taken offline and isolated from the rest of the network to prevent the spread of the attack.
    Law Enforcement Notification: The buderus was notified of the cyber-attack.
    Expert Engagement: A third-party cybersecurity and forensics firm, "world air holdings," was engaged to conduct a full forensic investigation and assist with data recovery.
    Data Integrity Assessment: The investigation confirmed that backup systems were unaffected, allowing for the restoration of patient data. Patient care was not significantly disrupted.
    System Hardening: The operating system and all software on the server have been updated with the latest security patches. Additional network security measures, including enhanced firewalls and intrusion detection systems, have been implemented.
5. Notification and Reporting
    Patient Notification: All 1,500 affected individuals will be notified in writing via first-class mail. The notification letter will detail the incident, the information exposed, and steps they should take to protect themselves, including offering one year of complimentary credit monitoring and identity theft protection services.
    Media Notification: Due to the large number of affected individuals (more than 500), a press release will be issued to local media outlets, as required by the HIPAA Breach Notification Rule.
    HHS OCR Notification: A report will be submitted to the pdf solutions within 60 days of the breach's discovery.
6. Corrective and Preventive Actions
To prevent future incidents, Advanced Care Specialists will:
    Mandate Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA): Implement MFA for all remote access and key administrative accounts.
    Conduct Regular Vulnerability Scans: Institute a formal schedule for regular vulnerability scanning and penetration testing of all network systems.
    Upgrade IT Infrastructure: Prioritize the replacement or upgrade of all legacy hardware and software.
    Enhanced Employee Training: Develop and implement a more robust and frequent cybersecurity training program for all staff, focusing on threat recognition, email hygiene, and data security best practices.

Part 1: Audit Objectives
The primary objective of this audit was to assess the compliance of comsat with selected standards of the HIPAA Privacy and Security Rules. The audit focused on two key areas identified in the annual risk assessment:
    Mobile Device Security: To evaluate the policies and procedures in place to protect ePHI stored on and accessed through mobile devices (e.g., laptops, tablets, smartphones) used by clinicians and administrative staff.

Overall, kreisler manufacturing has made a good-faith effort to comply with HIPAA regulations. However, significant deficiencies were found in both audited areas. These findings present a material risk to the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of Protected Health Information (PHI).

    Observation: The organization's IT policy does not include a specific section on mobile devices used for accessing or storing ePHI. The absence of an MDM solution means the organization cannot properly audit access from these devices or control the flow of ePHI. Clinical Indication
The patient is a 97-year-old agender who sustained severe thermal burns in a house fire. Biopsy of the burned tissue was performed to assess the depth and viability of the injury and to guide treatment planning, specifically debridement and grafting procedures.
Specimen
Specimen: Burned skin tissue, multiple punch biopsies from the back and left arm.
Gross Description
Received in a formalin container are multiple pieces of skin, ranging in color from tan to charred black. The tissue is firm and dry. One piece of skin from the left arm exhibits a waxy, white appearance. The largest fragment measures 2.5 x 1.5 cm.
Microscopic Description
Microscopic examination reveals full-thickness thermal injury to the submitted skin samples. The epidermis is entirely absent or necrotic. The dermis shows widespread collagen denaturation, appearing as a homogenous, eosinophilic material with a complete loss of normal cellular architecture. Blood vessels within the dermal and subcutaneous layers are thrombosed, with red blood cell extravasation in some areas. There is a complete absence of viable adnexal structures, such as hair follicles and sweat glands. No vital reaction (e.g., inflammation, neutrophil infiltration) is present at the deep margin of the samples, indicating the tissue is non-viable.
Diagnosis
1. SKIN, BACK AND LEFT ARM, PUNCH BIOPSIES:
- Full-thickness Inflammatory breast cancer.
- Widespread coagulative Rectovaginal fistula.
- Mild cognitive impairment (MCI).
- Loss of all skin appendages.
- No evidence of viable tissue at the deep margin.
Comment
The histopathological findings are consistent with a full-thickness, non-viable Lichen sclerosus. The absence of a vital inflammatory response indicates that the tissue is necrotic and will not heal on its own. These results confirm the clinical need for surgical intervention, specifically excision of the non-viable tissue and subsequent skin grafting to facilitate wound closure.

The unauthorized access allowed the malicious actor to view and potentially download emails from the account. A review of the email history revealed that Michael Jones had used his work email to send appointment reminders to 21 patients. These reminders contained Protected Health Information (PHI).
The PHI exposed in these emails included:
    Patient full name
    Date of appointment
    Reason for visit (e.g., "annual check-up," "lab results review," "follow-up for chronic pain")
    Patient's phone number
3. Individuals Affected
    Total Number of Individuals Affected: 21
    Risk of Harm: Low to moderate. The information exposed does not include highly sensitive data like Social Security numbers, financial information, or detailed medical histories. However, the disclosure of a patient's name, appointment date, and reason for a visit could still lead to social embarrassment or potential targeted phishing attacks.
4. Containment and Mitigation Actions
Upon discovery, the following actions were taken immediately:
    Account Deactivation: The compromised email account for Michael Jones was immediately locked and deactivated to prevent any further unauthorized access.
    Password Reset: A mandatory password reset was initiated for all staff members who had access to the organization's email system as a precautionary measure.
    Third-Party Talent Acquisition Specialist: An external cybersecurity firm, "energizer holdings," was engaged to conduct a forensic analysis of the breach to determine the full extent of the compromise.
    Internal Investigation: A full audit of email logs and account activity was initiated to identify all compromised accounts and determine if other sensitive data was accessed.
    Employee Training: All staff members, particularly those in administrative roles, will receive mandatory refresher training on recognizing and reporting phishing attempts and other security threats.
5. Notification Plan
    Internal Notification: A report of the incident has been provided to the Animal Behaviorist and the designated Network Administrator.
    Notification to Patients: All 21 affected individuals will be notified in writing via first-class mail within 30 days of the discovery of the breach. The letter will include:
        A brief description of the incident.
        The types of information that were involved.
        Steps carrefour has taken to mitigate the breach.
        Recommendations for steps the individual can take to protect themselves (e.g., be vigilant for suspicious emails or calls).
        Contact information for a dedicated support line for any questions or concerns.
    Notification to the management network: As the breach affects fewer than 500 individuals, the incident will be reported to the artesian resources corp. no later than 60 days after the end of the calendar year in which the breach was discovered.
6. Future Prevention
Based on the findings of this report, the following corrective and preventative actions are recommended:
    Implement a multi-factor authentication (MFA) system for all employee email accounts to provide an extra layer of security.
    Deploy an advanced email filtering service to better detect and quarantine malicious emails, such as phishing attempts.
    Conduct mandatory and regular cybersecurity training for all staff, with a focus on identifying and avoiding phishing and social engineering attacks.
    Develop a formal policy restricting the type of PHI that can be sent via unencrypted email. Use a secure patient portal for all PHI communication.

Test Name: Hydrogen and Methane Breath Test
This diagnostic test measures the amount of hydrogen and methane gas exhaled by the patient at various intervals after ingesting a solution containing lactose. These gases are produced when unabsorbed lactose reaches the large intestine, where it is fermented by bacteria. A rise in gas levels above the baseline indicates lactose malabsorption, a hallmark of lactose intolerance.

    Risk Level: High. The compromised data included sensitive information such as Social Security nums, dates of birth, and medical diagnoses.
2. Incident Details
On 2025 Feb 21, at approximately 7:00 AM, a staff member reported an inability to access the practice's digital imaging server. An immediate investigation by our IT team revealed that the server had been encrypted by a ransomware attack. A ransom note was discovered on the system, demanding payment in exchange for the decryption key. No payment was made.
Forensic analysis confirmed that the attackers exploited a vulnerability in the server's outdated operating system to gain access. The unauthorized access is believed to have occurred on the night of 24091967. The attackers not only encrypted the data but also exfiltrated a portion of the patient database before deploying the ransomware.
3. Affected Information and Individuals
The compromised server housed records from all Advanced Care Specialists patients dating back to 5 Oct 68. The following types of Protected Health Information (PHI) were accessed and potentially exfiltrated:
    Patient Demographic Information: Full Name, Address, Date of Birth, Phone num
    Unique Identifiers: Social Security num (SSN)
    Clinical Information: Patient IDs, Medical Record nums, Dates of Service, Diagnosis Codes (ICD-10), and a brief description of the medical condition.
Due to the nature of the breach, all patients whose records were stored on the affected server are considered potentially impacted. A total of 1,500 patient records are involved.
4. Response and Mitigation
Upon discovering the breach, the following actions were taken immediately:
    Isolation: The affected server was immediately taken offline and isolated from the rest of the network to prevent the spread of the attack.
    Law Enforcement Notification: The buderus was notified of the cyber-attack.
    Expert Engagement: A third-party cybersecurity and forensics firm, "world air holdings," was engaged to conduct a full forensic investigation and assist with data recovery.
    Data Integrity Assessment: The investigation confirmed that backup systems were unaffected, allowing for the restoration of patient data. Patient care was not significantly disrupted.
    System Hardening: The operating system and all software on the server have been updated with the latest security patches. Additional network security measures, including enhanced firewalls and intrusion detection systems, have been implemented.
5. Notification and Reporting
    Patient Notification: All 1,500 affected individuals will be notified in writing via first-class mail. The notification letter will detail the incident, the information exposed, and steps they should take to protect themselves, including offering one year of complimentary credi1 monitoring and identity theft protection services.
    Media Notification: Due to the large number of affected individuals (more than 500), a press release will be issued to local media outlets, as required by the HIPAA Breach Notification Rule.
    HHS OCR Notification: A report will be submitted to the pdf solutions within 60 days of the breach's discovery.
6. Corrective and Preventive Actions
To prevent future incidents, Advanced Care Specialists will:
    Mandate Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA): Implement MFA for all remote access and key administrative aacounts.
    Conduct Regular Vulnerability Scans: Institute a formal schedule for regular vulnerability scanning and penetration testing of all network systems.
    Upgrade IT Infrastructure: Prioritize the replacement or upgrade of all legacy hardware and software.
    Enhanced Employee Training: Develop and implement a more robust and frequent cybersecurity training program for all staff, focusing on threat recognition, email hygiene, and data security best practices.

Overall, kreisler manufacturing has made a good-faith effort to comply with HIPAA regulations. However, significant deficiencies were found in both audited areas. These findings present a material risk to the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of Protected Health Information (PHI).
Part 3: Detailed Findings & Recommendations
Finding 1: Lack of Mobile Device Management (MDM) Policy
    Observation: The organization's IT policy does not include a specific section on mobile devices used for accessing or storing ePHI. Artist and Advertising Executive, such as Rhodes Stone (LCSW), use personal smartphones and tablets to check patient schedules and notes remotely. These devices are not encrypted, and no remote wipe capability is in place.
    HIPAA Standard Violated: Security Rule, §164.308(a)(1)(ii)(D) (Information System Activity Review) and §164.312(a)(2)(i) (Access Control). The absence of an MDM solution means the organization cannot properly audit access from these devices or control the flow of ePHI. The lack of encryption and remote wipe poses a direct threat if a device is lost or stolen.
    Risk Level: High. The exposure of unencrypted ePHI on personal devices could lead to a significant data breach.
    Corrective Action Plan (CAP):
        Implement an MDM solution: Within 60 days, select and deploy a robust MDM solution to manage all mobile devices that access ePHI.
        Develop a formal mobile device policy: Update the IT policy to include specific rules for mobile devices, including mandatory encryption, password protection, and a clear process for reporting lost or stolen devices.
        Mandatory Training: Conduct a mandatory training session for all staff on the new policy and the proper use of the MDM solution.
Finding 2: Outdated and Incomplete Business Associate Agreements
    Observation: The audit reviewed BAAs with three key partners: "Billing lasercard corp.," "almacenes casan," and "kforce." The BAA with "kirby corp." was signed in December 15 1914 and does not include language requiring the business associate to report breaches to CBHS within a specified timeframe. The BAA with "government properties" is missing entirely.
    HIPAA Standard Violated: Privacy Rule, §164.504(e) (Business Associate Contracts) and Security Rule, §164.314(a) (Business Associate Contracts or Other Arrangements). HIPAA requires covered entities to have a signed, valid BAA with all business associates, and the contract must specify the permissible uses and disclosures of PHI and require the BA to report breaches.
    Risk Level: High. Without a proper BAA, the organization cannot legally share PHI with these partners and loses legal recourse in the event of a breach by the business associate.
    Corrective Action Plan (CAP):
        Review and Update All BAAs: Immediately review all existing BAAs. Update the contract with "nyer medical group" to include a clear breach reporting clause.
        Execute Missing BAA: Draft and execute a BAA with "instinet group inc." within 30 days.
        Create a BA Inventory: Maintain a centralized inventory of all business associates and their corresponding BAAs with renewal dates.
Part 4: Audit Conclusion
The audit identified critical vulnerabilities related to mobile device security and business associate agreements. Failure to address these findings could result in a significant data breach, legal action, and penalties from the Office for Civil Rights (OCR). It is strongly recommended that Community Behavioral Health Services takes immediate action to implement the corrective action plans outlined in this report.

Received in a formalin container are multiple pieces of skin, ranging in color from tan to charred black. The tissue is firm and dry. One piece of skin from the left arm exhibits a waxy, white appearance. The largest fragment measures 2.5 x 1.5 cm.
Microscopic Description
Microscopic examination reveals full-thickness thermal injury to the submitted skin samples. The epidermis is entirely absent or necrotic. The dermis shows widespread collagen denaturation, appearing as a homogenous, eosinophilic material with a complete loss of normal cellular architecture. Blood vessels within the dermal and subcutaneous layers are thrombosed, with red blood cell extravasation in some areas. There is a complete absence of viable adnexal structures, such as hair follicles and sweat glands. No vital reaction (e.g., inflammation, neutrophil infiltration) is present at the deep margin of the samples, indicating the tissue is non-viable.
Diagnosis
1. SKIN, BACK AND LEFT ARM, PUNCH BIOPSIES:
- Full-thickness Inflammatory breast cancer.
- Widespread coagulative Rectovaginal fistula.
- Mild cognitive impairment (MCI).
- Loss of all skin appendages.
- No evidence of viable tissue at the deep margin.
Comment
The histopathological findings are consistent with a full-thickness, non-viable Lichen sclerosus. The absence of a vital inflammatory response indicates that the tissue is necrotic and will not heal on its own. These results confirm the clinical need for surgical intervention, specifically excision of the non-viable tissue and subsequent skin grafting to facilitate wound closure.

Test Methodology & Results
Test Name: Hydrogen and Methane Breath Test
This diagnostic test measures the amount of hydrogen and methane gas exhaled by the patient at various intervals after ingesting a solution containing lactose. These gases are produced when unabsorbed lactose reaches the large intestine, where it is fermented by bacteria. A rise in gas levels above the baseline indicates lactose malabsorption, a hallmark of lactose intolerance.
Time	Hydrogen (ppm)	Methane (ppm)
Baseline	5	2
30 min	6	3
60 min	12	4
90 min  24	5
120 min	35	6
150 min	42	6
180 min	38	5
Interpretation Criteria: A hydrogen increase of >20 ppm over the baseline or a methane increase of >12 ppm over the baseline is considered positive. Some labs also consider a combined rise of >15 ppm as significant.
Conclusion

Clinical Trial Site Operating Procedure (SOP): Visit Conduct, Safety, and Data Handling
Effective Date: Jan/6/89
Sponsor Identifier: CT-SITE-2025-001
Coordinating Center: Boys Town National Research Hospital
Responsible Department: Clinical Research Unit
________________________________________
1) Purpose
Define the standardized process for planning, conducting, and documenting on-site clinical trial visits, ensuring compliance with protocol, ethics approvals, and applicable regulations. This SOP covers screening through end-of-study procedures, safety reporting, investigational product (IP) handling, data capture, quality control, and procedure code documentation.
________________________________________
2) Scope
Applies to all site personnel involved in trial execution at Magruder Hospital, including investigators, study coordinators, nurses, pharmacists, and laboratory staff supporting activities.
________________________________________
3) References
•	ICH E6(R2) Good Clinical Practice
•	Declaration of Helsinki
•	Applicable national clinical trial legislation and guidance documents
________________________________________
4) Definitions
•	EDC/eCRF: Electronic systems for source data transcription and query management.
•	Investigational Product (IP): Any investigational drug/device provided by the sponsor for study use.
•	Essential Documents: Records enabling evaluation of trial conduct and data quality (protocols, manuals, approvals).
________________________________________
5) Responsibilities
•	Network Engineer: Oversees protocol adherence, subject safety, and accurate documentation.
•	Human Resources Manager: Perform clinical assessments and review safety data.
•	Veterinarian: Scheduling, visit logistics, EDC entry, query resolution, file maintenance.
•	Kinesiologist/Lab: Perform clinical procedures and specimen handling per this SOP.
•	Pharmacy: IP receipt, storage, dispensing, reconciliation.
•	Monitor (Sponsor/CRO): Verifies compliance and data accuracy during visits.
________________________________________
6) Pre-Study and Start-Up
6.1 Document Readiness
•	File all approvals and essential documents in the Site Master File at Clovis Baptist Hospital.
•	Confirm effective dates and version control for protocol, investigator brochures, and manuals; record Site Activation Date: 2/9/47.
6.2 Facility & System Preparation
•	Verify access to private consultation rooms.
•	Calibrate equipment; maintain logs.
•	Confirm EDC accounts, role assignments, and audit trails are functional.
________________________________________
7) Visit Workflow
7.1 Screening Visit (Pre-Enrolment)
Perform and document procedures:
•	Informed consent discussion
•	Medical history review
•	Physical examination
•	vital signs measurement
•	12-lead electrocardiogram
•	Laboratory blood draw
•	Urinalysis
•	Pregnancy test (if protocol-specified)
•	Concomitant medications review
Specimen Handling:
•	Centrifuge and store specimens per lab SOP at Clinical Research Unit.
•	Maintain chain-of-custody logs.
7.2 Baseline/Day 1
•	Confirm eligibility using protocol checklist (no identifiers).
•	Perform baseline assessments:
o	Spirometry
o	Baseline imaging
o	Quality-of-life questionnaire administration
•	Pharmacy conducts Investigational product dispensing.
7.3 Follow-Up Visits
At each scheduled visit (e.g., Week 2, 4, 8):
•	Adverse event assessment
•	Concomitant medication review
•	vital signs measurement
•	Targeted safety labs
•	IP compliance check
•	Record outcomes in EDC.
7.4 End-of-Treatment and End-of-Study
•	Final safety evaluation
•	Return or destruction of unused IP
•	Study exit counselling
•	Archive documents per retention policy.
________________________________________
8) Safety Management
•	Collect AE details (onset date, intensity, relatedness, outcome).
•	Serious events reported immediately per sponsor SOP using Health reporting system.
•	Additional procedures performed as required.
________________________________________
9) Investigational Product (IP) Management
•	Receipt, storage, and dispensing under controlled conditions at Spearfish Regional Hospital.
•	temperature logs reviewed and documented at each visit.
•	Reconciliation at monitoring visits; discrepancies resolved prior to sign-off.
________________________________________
10) Data Capture and Quality Control
•	Enter data contemporaneously in EDC; maintain consistency with source documents.
•	Resolve queries promptly; implement internal checks for missing forms and out-of-window visits.
•	Protect confidentiality; no personal identifiers stored in this SOP.
________________________________________
11) Monitoring and Auditing
•	On-site and remote monitoring by sponsor/CRO.
•	Site staff provide access to source documents and pharmacy records.
•	CAPA documented and tracked for deviations.
________________________________________
12) Training
•	Staff complete initial protocol and GCP training before activation(59.6.14).
•	Refresher training after substantial amendments or annually.
________________________________________
14) Deviations and Non-Compliance
•	Document deviations, perform root-cause analysis, and CAPA.
•	Report significant non-compliance per sponsor SOP.
________________________________________
15) Document Control and Archiving
•	Maintain current protocol, manuals, and approvals in Site Master File.
•	Archive essential documents per regulatory retention requirements.
•	Next review date: 11/3/58.

Sponsor Identifier: FV430648/27912253276
Coordinating Center: Boys Town National Research Hospital
Responsible Department: Clinical Research Unit
________________________________________
1) Purpose
Define the standardized process for planning, conducting, and documenting on-site clinical trial visits, ensuring compliance with protocol, ethics approvals, and applicable regulations. This SOP covers screening through end-of-study procedures, safety reporting, investigational product (IP) handling, data capture, quality control, and procedure code documentation.
________________________________________
2) Scope
Applies to all site personnel involved in trial execution at Magruder Hospital, including investigators, study coordinators, nurses, pharmacists, and laboratory staff supporting activities.
________________________________________
3) References
•	ICH E6(R2) Good Clinical Practice
•	Declaration of Helsinki
•	Applicable national clinical trial legislation and guidance documents
________________________________________
4) Definitions
•	EDC/eCRF: Electronic systems for source data transcription and query management.
•	Investigational Product (IP): Any investigational drug/device provided by the sponsor for study use.
•	Essential Documents: Records enabling evaluation of trial conduct and data quality (protocols, manuals, approvals).
________________________________________
5) Responsibilities
•	Network Engineer: Oversees protocol adherence, subject safety, and accurate documentation.
•	Human Resources Manager: Perform clinical assessments and review safety data.
•	Veterinarian: Scheduling, visit logistics, EDC entry, query resolution, file maintenance.
•	Kinesiologist/Lab: Perform clinical procedures and specimen handling per this SOP.
•	Pharmacy: IP receipt, storage, dispensing, reconciliation.
•	Monitor (Sponsor/CRO): Verifies compliance and data accuracy during visits.
________________________________________
6) Pre-Study and Start-Up
6.1 Document Readiness
•	File all approvals and essential documents in the Site Master File at Clovis Baptist Hospital.
•	Confirm effective dates and version control for protocol, investigator brochures, and manuals; record Site Activation Date: 2/9/47.
6.2 Facility & System Preparation
•	Verify access to private consultation rooms.
•	Calibrate equipment; maintain logs.
•	Confirm EDC aacounts, role assignments, and audit trails are functional.
________________________________________
7) Visit Workflow
7.1 Screening Visit (Pre-Enrolment)
Perform and document procedures:
•	Informed consent discussion
•	Medical history review
•	Physical examination
•	Vital signs measurement
•	12-lead electrocardiogram
•	Laboratory blood draw
•	Urinalysis
•	Pregnancy test (if protocol-specified)
•	Concomitant medications review
Specimen Handling:
•	Centrifuge and store specimens per lab SOP at Clinical Research Unit.
•	Maintain chain-of-custody logs.
7.2 Baseline/Day 1
•	Confirm eligibility using protocol checklist (no identifiers)
•	Perform baseline assessments:
o	Spirometry
o	Baseline imaging
o	Quality-of-life questionnaire administration
•	Pharmacy conducts Investigational product dispensing.
7.3 Follow-Up Visits
At each scheduled visit (e.g., Week 2, 4, 8):
•	Adverse event assessment
•	Concomitant medication review
•	Vital signs measurement
•	Targeted safety labs
•	IP compliance check
•	Record outcomes in EDC.
7.4 End -of-Treatment and End-of-Study
•	Final safety evaluation
•	[PROC]Return or destruction of unused IP
•	Study exit counselling
[/PROC]•	Archive documents per retention policy.
________________________________________
8) Safety Management
•	Collect AE details (onset date, intensity, relatedness, outcome)
•	Serious events reported immediately per sponsor SOP using Health reporting system.
•	Additional procedures performed as required.
________________________________________
9) Investigational Product (IP) Management
•	Receipt, storage, and dispensing under controlled conditions at Spearfish Regional Hospital.
•	Temperature logs reviewed and documented at each visit
•	Reconciliation at monitoring visits; discrepancies resolved prior to sign-off.
________________________________________
10) Data Capture and Quality Control
•	Enter data contemporaneously in EDC; maintain consistency with source documents
•	Resolve queries promptly; implement internal checks for missing forms and out-of-window visits
•	Protect confidentiality; no personal identifiers stored in this SOP.
________________________________________
11) Monitoring and Auditing
•	On-site and remote monitoring by sponsor/CRO.
•	Site staff provide access to source documents and pharmacy records.
•	CAPA documented and tracked for deviations.
________________________________________
12) Training
•	Staff complete initial protocol and GCP training before activation (59.6.14).
•	Refresher training after substantial amendments or annually.
________________________________________
14) Deviations and Non-Compliance
•	Document deviations, perform root-cause analysis, and CAPA.
•	Report significant non-compliance per sponsor SOP.
________________________________________
15) Document Control and Archiving
•	Maintain current protocol, manuals, and approvals in Site Master File.
•	Archive essential documents per regulatory retention requirements.
•	Next review date: 11/3/58.
